account: Today I have followed my appointments: the morning market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and now three o'clock tea with my neighbour at the dockside cottage. I am due back at the office at half past four. I have asked residents and the secretary for news, but have not yet learned of anything clearly improper or unusual. Several residents reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later a sack of bread at the inn and plaza_north_1. Those reports could simply reflect baking and deliveries; I have no evidence of another purpose. The builder reported that the bridge is passable, lanterns are present, and no defects or repairs are confirmed. He subsequently requested a two-emerald inspection fee that had not been agreed in advance. I declined retrospective approval and asked the secretary to record that no repairs or fee were authorized. Much of our conversation was difficult to hear, so his repeated requests may reflect missed replies rather than anything more. As I left town hall, I directly saw freight give the secretary a written book. I do not know its contents or purpose; it might be ordinary town business, but it is worth asking about when I return. My neighbour has heard my greeting and question about east-bank news, but has not yet replied. I still have a feeling that there may be town affairs I am missing, but so far I cannot identify a secret undertaking, its participants, or its purpose.
